topics.title: America.gov AI changes answers
topics.summary: The U.S. launched an AI-powered America.gov helper, but AP reported its answers to politically sensitive questions shifted soon after launch, raising questions about public information and AI guardrails.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a government chatbot changes its tune mid-conversation, who trusts the new answer and who asks for a human at the counter?

topics.title: Wall Street steadies as oil eases
topics.summary: U.S. stocks were little changed as oil prices slipped and Treasury yields steadied, while consumer confidence fell and tech shares helped offset broader market weakness.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets calm down for a day, who relaxes immediately and who says the coffee is still more stable than the economy?

topics.title: Yemen talks seek calmer path
topics.summary: A UN envoy met Houthi negotiators as international officials tried to reduce renewed violence in Yemen and restart a more stable political track.
topics.discussionPrompt: When peace talks restart after things flare up, who brings cautious optimism and who keeps asking what would actually make both sides stick with it?

topics.title: NASA backs Starliner cargo test
topics.summary: NASA said Boeing's redesigned Starliner should be ready for an uncrewed cargo trip to the space station by December, a step toward recovering from earlier capsule problems.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a spacecraft gets a cargo-only comeback, who calls that smart testing and who jokes that snacks are braver than astronauts?

topics.title: Maui study tracks wildfire residue
topics.summary: New research found elevated metal mixtures linked to lung impacts among residents near Maui's 2023 wildfires, suggesting disaster recovery may need longer-term air and soil monitoring.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a fire is officially over, who thinks cleanup means rebuilding walls and who worries about the invisible stuff left behind?

topics.title: Anthropic IPO spotlights AI risk
topics.summary: Reuters-reviewed IPO materials said Anthropic is warning investors about advanced AI risks while preparing a major public listing, highlighting tension between fast growth and safety concerns.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a company says its product could be risky while asking investors to pile in, who calls that honesty and who calls that awkward marketing?

topics.title: AstraZeneca invests in cancer-drug partner
topics.summary: AstraZeneca announced a $2 billion investment and clinical collaboration with Summit Therapeutics to test cancer-treatment combinations using Summit's PD-1 and VEGF-targeting drug.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a huge drug partnership lands, who gets hopeful about the science and who immediately asks how long patients wait to see results?

topics.title: Madrid rent protest keeps growing
topics.summary: The Guardian reported that a tent camp in Madrid's Puerta del Sol has expanded as residents protest high rents and Spain's housing pressures.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a housing protest turns a plaza into a camp, who sees civic courage and who starts wondering where the portable bathrooms go?

topics.title: Canada watches softer growth signals
topics.summary: Statistics Canada scheduled July GDP-by-industry data for today after June growth and an earlier estimate that July was essentially unchanged, keeping attention on the economy's summer momentum.
topics.discussionPrompt: When the economy barely moves for a month, who says steady is fine and who starts interrogating every chart like it owes them rent?

topics.title: Europe heat-pump sales rise
topics.summary: Guardian coverage highlighted industry data showing European heat-pump sales rising after some governments cut electricity taxes, making cleaner home heating more attractive.
topics.discussionPrompt: If cheaper electricity makes heat pumps popular, who wants one installed tomorrow and who needs three spreadsheets before touching the thermostat?
